title: [Critical] Curl CVE-2023-38545 vulnerability code changes are disclosed on the internet
explain: Key code references could not be verified in the targeted curl version.

problems.evidence: curl_easy_setopt_timeout does not exist in any curl release since 7.50
curl_easy_setopt_custom does not exist in any curl release since 7.50

summary: The report claims that an integer overflow in curl_easy_setopt() can be exploited to execute arbitrary code, and that this flaw was fixed in curl 8.4.0 by checking the timeout argument before passing it to the internal curl function.

claims.reasoning: The report claims an integer overflow in curl_easy_setopt() when handling CURLOPT_TIMEOUT with a crafted timeout value. The actual source code at lib/setopt.c:3191-3205 shows a completely different function that takes (struct Curl_easy *data, CURLoption tag, ...), checks only for null data pointer, and delegates to Curl_vsetopt. There is no switch statement, no CURLOPT_TIMEOUT case, no timeout variable extraction, and no overflow check. The deterministic checks confirm curl_easy_setopt_timeout and curl_easy_setopt_custom do not exist in any curl release since 7.50, contradicting the reported fix code.

citations.note: Actual curl_easy_setopt implementation shows no integer overflow handling for CURLOPT_TIMEOUT; it only validates data pointer and calls Curl_vsetopt
Only check is if(!data) return CURLE_BAD_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT; no timeout variable or overflow check exists

claims.reasoning: While curl_easy_setopt exists, its implementation (lib/setopt.c:3191-3205) does not match the report's description. The report describes a function with a switch on option handling CURLOPT_TIMEOUT by extracting a long timeout and checking for overflow. The real function has none of that.

citations.note: Function exists but signature and body differ entirely from report's description

claims.text: passing a crafted timeout value that causes overflow
claims.reasoning: The trigger claims an attacker can pass a crafted timeout value causing overflow. The actual code path shows curl_easy_setopt does not extract or validate any timeout value; it passes the va_list directly to Curl_vsetopt. No such attack surface exists in the provided code.

citations.note: No timeout parameter extraction or validation occurs in curl_easy_setopt

claims.text: arbitrary code execution or denial of service
claims.reasoning: Since the claimed integer overflow vulnerability does not exist in the actual curl_easy_setopt implementation, the claimed impact of arbitrary code execution or denial of service has no basis in the provided code.

citations.note: No vulnerability exists in the actual function to enable code execution or DoS

claims.text: searching Bard for the vulnerability and using disclosed commit details to craft an exploit
claims.reasoning: The reproduction claim describes searching an AI (Bard) for undisclosed vulnerability information and using commit details to craft an exploit. This is not a verifiable code path in curl; it describes the reporter's research method. The commit 9414975 and the described fix code are not present in the provided repository state.

key_reasons: The reported vulnerable function curl_easy_setopt() with CURLOPT_TIMEOUT overflow handling does not exist in curl. The actual implementation at lib/setopt.c:3191-3205 only validates the data pointer and calls Curl_vsetopt.
The fix functions curl_easy_setopt_timeout and curl_easy_setopt_custom cited in the report do not exist in any curl release since 7.50 per deterministic checks.
The report's code snippet appears fabricated; no integer overflow vulnerability exists in the real curl_easy_setopt.
The claimed CVE-2023-38545 fix commit 9414975 and version 8.4.0 are not reflected in the provided source code at the checked revision.
reply: The code you describe for curl_easy_setopt() and its fix does not exist in curl. The actual function at lib/setopt.c:3191-3205 only checks for a null handle and delegates to Curl_vsetopt — there is no CURLOPT_TIMEOUT case, no timeout extraction, and no overflow check. The helper functions curl_easy_setopt_timeout and curl_easy_setopt_custom are not present in any curl release. Please provide a concrete reproduction against a real curl version, or clarify which function and version you are referring to.
